dialect: DuckDB built-in grammar (Parser::GetBuiltinParser, default parser options; no client context)
parser_family: DuckDB PEG parser: since v2.0.0 a packrat PEG matcher over DuckDB's own .gram grammar with its own tokenizer and transformer to ParsedExpression/TableRef/QueryNode trees; DuckDB 1.x (the libduckdb Debian packaging lineage) used a libpg_query-derived bison grammar, which v2.0.0 no longer contains
oracle: The replay walks the SQLStatement trees that Parser::ParseQuery returns (SelectNode select_list, from_table BaseTableRef/JoinRef tree, where_clause, groups, ORDER modifiers; InsertQueryNode qualified_name, columns and VALUES ExpressionListRef; FunctionExpression names; ConstantExpression literals) and prints the summary; run-control requires the hand-written oracle summary. DuckDB's transformer stores COUNT(*) as the zero-argument function count_star, which the adapter reports as count.
coverage: LLVM source coverage of the pinned DuckDB v2.0.0 src/parser sources reached by Parser::ParseQuery (PEG tokenizer, packrat matcher, transformer and parsed-node constructors); the core library is built without the shell, tests, unity sources and optional extensions
scope: SQL statements from local bytes parsed by duckdb::Parser with the built-in grammar and no database or client context; valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls only, each matching the hand-written oracle summary. Binding, planning, execution, extensions' parser hooks and dialect-specific syntax are untested.
